To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and developed an innovative bifunctional antibody-based drug-delivery system that can deliver imaging or therapeutic radiolabeled or nonradioactive agents to a tumor while minimizing the dose of these agents to normal tissue.

we have designed, synthesized, and evaluated a bifunctional monoclonal antibody that delivers a radioisotope selectively to tumors, with minimal radiation exposure of normal tissue, for imaging of tumors.
the bifunctional antibody is a new binary drug delivery system that is effective in imaging colorectal cancer and may have potential for the treatment of this and other malignancies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new drug delivery system that can be applied to the delivery of a variety of agents to a tumor site.
the development of a new class of monoclonal antibodies for use in tumor imaging and therapy.
the development of a new approach to cancer therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this new drug delivery system, bifunctional antibody (BFA), is a safe, effective, and practical method to deliver imaging agents and therapeutic agents to tumor sites.
